claims.reason: `Memℓp.neg` and `Memℓp.star_mem` have the same three-way split on `p`, and each branch uses only that the pointwise norm is unchanged. `Memℓp.mono'` (stated earlier in the same namespace) already handles all exponents from a pointwise norm bound. It needs only `hg : Memℓp g p` and `∀ i, ‖f i‖ ≤ ‖g i‖`, and it uses the earlier `memℓp_norm_iff` alias. Instantiating it with `g := f` therefore gives both lemmas, with no dependency cycle and no new hypotheses. `star_mem` is stated in a context with `NormedStarGroup (E i)`, which supplies `norm_star`. The change removes two copies of the case analysis and states the real reason the property is preserved.
claims.shared_lemma: Memℓp.mono' {F : α → Type*} [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (F i)] {f : (i : α) → E i} {g : (i : α) → F i} (hg : Memℓp g p) (hfg : ∀ i, ‖f i‖ ≤ ‖g i‖) : Memℓp f p  -- already in the file
rewritten_uses: theorem neg {f : ∀ i, E i} (hf : Memℓp f p) : Memℓp (-f) p := hf.mono' fun i => by simp
theorem _root_.Memℓp.star_mem {f : ∀ i, E i} (hf : Memℓp f p) : Memℓp (star f) p := hf.mono' fun i => by simp  -- via norm_star

theorem _root_.Memℓp.star_mem {f : ∀ i, E i} (hf : Memℓp f p) : Memℓp (star f) p := by
  rcases p.trichotomy with (rfl | rfl | hp)
  · apply memℓp_zero
    simp [hf.finite_dsupport]

theorem mono' {F : α → Type*} [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (F i)] {f : (i : α) → E i}
    {g : (i : α) → F i} (hg : Memℓp g p) (hfg : ∀ i, ‖f i‖ ≤ ‖g i‖) :
    Memℓp f p :=
  hg.norm.mono hfg

claims.reason: `lp.norm_toNorm` already proves, by a case split on `p`, that the `lp` norm equals the norm of the sequence of pointwise norms. `lp.norm_neg` and the `NormedStarGroup (lp E p)` instance redo the same split. `norm_neg` also repeats the empty-index case with `IsLUB.unique` and `HasSum.unique`. The star instance adds an impossible `p = 0` branch. A lemma stating that the norm depends only on `fun i => ‖x i‖`, placed after `norm_toNorm`, gives both. Its proof is `toNorm x = toNorm y` by `ext`/`funext`, then two rewrites with `norm_toNorm`. The `norm_toNorm` proof uses only `norm_eq_card_dsupport`, `norm_eq_ciSup` and `norm_eq_tsum_rpow`, which come earlier, so there is no cycle. The lemma needs no `p ≠ 0` or `Fact (1 ≤ p)` hypothesis, so the star instance no longer needs its `exfalso` branch. The two uses become one-liners, and the case analysis lives in one place.
claims.shared_lemma: lp.norm_eq_of_norm_apply_eq {F : α → Type*} [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (F i)] {x : lp E p} {y : lp F p} (h : ∀ i, ‖x i‖ = ‖y i‖) : ‖x‖ = ‖y‖  -- proof: have : toNorm x = toNorm y := lp.ext (funext h); rw [← norm_toNorm (x := x), ← norm_toNorm (x := y), this]
rewritten_uses: theorem norm_neg ⦃f : lp E p⦄ : ‖-f‖ = ‖f‖ := norm_eq_of_norm_apply_eq fun i => by simp
instance [hp : Fact (1 ≤ p)] : NormedStarGroup (lp E p) where norm_star_le f := le_of_eq (norm_eq_of_norm_apply_eq fun i => by simp)  -- via lp.star_apply and norm_star
